mainEntity.name: Does IPP offer full chemical plants for sale?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. In addition to individual equipment, we sell complete chemical process plants, including teardown and relocation services.

mainEntity.name: Can I inspect the equipment before buying?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. IPP offers on-site and video inspections for most equipment. Contact us to schedule one.

mainEntity.name: Where does IPP source its chemical equipment?

acceptedAnswer.text: From multinational chemical producers, toll manufacturers and decommissioned or restructured facilities worldwide.

mainEntity.name: What is chemical process plant equipment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chemical process plant equipment is the set of reactors, heat exchangers, centrifuges, dryers, filters, columns and tanks that converts raw materials into chemical products. Read IPP’s chemical process plant equipment guide.

mainEntity.name: How do I get a price for a chemical plant or equipment?

acceptedAnswer.text: We quote each plant and unit individually. Contact IPP with the stock number or your process requirements. The quotation defines the assets included and any dismantling, loading, shipping or start-up services.

mainEntity.name: Can IPP help with international shipping?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We coordinate packaging, crating, freight and delivery, or buyers can arrange their own shipping. Confirm the asset location, loading requirements and destination when you request a quotation.

mainEntity.name: What documentation is available for a used plant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Documentation varies by asset. We share the equipment lists, drawings, process descriptions and inspection records available for each plant or stock number.
Yes. IPP advertises financing for its plants and equipment. Contact IPP to discuss terms for your purchase.

mainEntity.name: Does IPP sell new chemical process equipment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Gale Process Solutions (GPS), an IPP group company, fabricates new stainless steel process equipment with 12 to 16 week average delivery. Universal Glasteel Equipment (UGE) supplies new and re-glassed glass-lined equipment.

mainEntity.name: Does IPP buy shutdown chemical plants and surplus equipment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We buy complete plants, process lines and individual equipment from shutdown, idled and restructured sites. Start with the sell a plant or sell equipment form.

mainEntity.name: What information should I provide when selling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Provide an asset list, photographs, the plant location, available technical documents and your removal deadline. Our team reviews the information and confirms the next steps.

mainEntity.name: Does IPP buy the land and buildings with a chemical plant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. IPP purchases complete plant sites, including the land, buildings, equipment and intellectual property. We also buy individual process units and equipment systems within a site. Read how selling to IPP works.

mainEntity.name: Does IPP assume environmental obligations at a plant site?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in some acquisitions. IPP buys sites with known contamination and assumes site cleanup and regulatory compliance obligations as the buyer. Our remediation partners work with local environmental authorities on each site. Discuss a site exit with IPP.

mainEntity.name: Which companies sell chemical plants to IPP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fortune 100 and Fortune 500 companies typically represent 95% of the sellers IPP works with, according to IPP. IPP occasionally buys assets from smaller manufacturers in distressed situations.

mainEntity.name: Does IPP buy equipment as-is, where-is?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. IPP buys used, surplus and idled equipment as-is, where-is, as a principal buyer rather than a broker. Our team arranges inspection, dismantling, packaging, freight and export.

mainEntity.name: Can IPP market a plant instead of buying it outright?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. IPP proposes either an outright purchase or a marketing arrangement that offers the assets to its global buyer network. IPP markets BASF’s ammonia, methanol and melamine plants at Ludwigshafen under such an agreement.

mainEntity.name: Does IPP handle decommissioning and dismantling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Our team decommissions and dismantles the plant, then packs, ships and exports the equipment. IPP holds ISN RAVS Plus verification for plant decommissioning work.

mainEntity.name: What happens to a chemical plant site after a sale?

acceptedAnswer.text: The purchase agreement defines the outcome. A sale can cover equipment for removal or the entire site, and our published projects include equipment relocation and site repurposing.
